title: Real Footage of a One Ton Rover Landing on Mars
description: Cameras on board the Perseverance rover captured its entry, descent, and touchdown in Jezero Crater. This is the first time a landing on another planet was recorded as it happened.
hook_card: Seven minutes of terror on Mars.

shots.narration: In February 2021, a spacecraft approached Jezero Crater, once the site of an ancient lake and river delta.
The craft hit the top of the Martian atmosphere at about 20,000 kilometres per hour.
Radio signals took about eleven minutes to reach Earth, delaying news of the seven-minute entry and landing.
The landing was already over before mission control could hear about it on Earth.
A 21.5-metre parachute opened while the craft was still supersonic, spelling Dare Mighty Things in binary code.
A rocket-powered descent stage hovered and lowered the rover using 7.6-metre cables.
Cameras on the craft filmed the landing on another planet for the very first time.
The descent stage flew off to crash a safe distance away after lowering the 1,025-kilogram rover.
On 18 February 2021, Perseverance landed safely on Mars, weighing roughly the same as a small car.
